question.problem:
$$
a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,P=\frac{1}{18}[\begin{aligned}{p}_{11} & {p}_{12} & {p}_{13} \\ {p}_{21} & {p}_{22} & {p}_{23} \\ {p}_{31} & {p}_{32} & {p}_{33}\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that the vector $a$ above spans ${S}^{⊥},$ and that $P$ is the orthogonal projection matrix of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace $S$, what is the value of ${p}_{23}+{p}_{31}?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the orthogonal projection matrix onto ${S}^{⊥}=\text{Span}\{a\}.$

Using the formula for the orthogonal projection matrix

$$
{P}_{{S}^{⊥}}=a({a}^{T}\,a)^{-1}{a}^{T},
$$

we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{{S}^{⊥}} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & ={18}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{18}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -4 \\ -1 & 1 & 4 \\ -4 & 4 & 16\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that ${P}_{S}+{P}_{{S}^{⊥}}=I.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =I-{P}_{{S}^{⊥}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{18}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -4 \\ -1 & 1 & 4 \\ -4 & 4 & 16\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{18}[\begin{aligned}17 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 17 & -4 \\ 4 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${p}_{23}+{p}_{31}=(-4)+4=0.$
